::: {.piege packages="lubridate"}
```{r}
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(lubridate))

duration("1h 32m 6s")
period("1h 32m 6s")
duration("01:32:06")
hours(4.7)
```
:::

## Why

When {lubridate} parses a duration written as text, lowercase `m` stands for months and uppercase `M` for minutes. `"1h 32m 6s"` is therefore one hour, 32 months and 6 seconds: more than two and a half years. The period's printout does say so in its own way, `32m 0d 1H 0M 6S`, but you have to know how to read it.

The other spellings fare no better: `duration()` does not understand the clock format `"01:32:06"` and returns `NA` without a warning. Finally, a period (`hours()`, `minutes()`...) counts calendar units and rejects decimals, with an unhelpful S4 object validation message.

## The remedy

Write `min` for minutes, parse the clock format with `hms()`, and go through durations (`dhours()`, in exact seconds) for decimal quantities.

::: {.piege packages="lubridate"}
```{r}
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(lubridate))

duration("1h 32min 6s")
as.duration(hms("01:32:06"))
dhours(4.7)
```
:::
